SMTO-HTTP-0042 — The service's sign-in reply wasn't one SMTO expected

GUID: 177ec776-aef0-4577-b44e-1ecb9405e2e9
Slug: http-auth-http-error
Domain: HTTP · Subsystem: http

What happened

  • The sign-in answered with a result this connection isn't set up to count as success, such as sending SMTO on to another page. Your details aren't necessarily wrong.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open Parameter Store, select the HTTP connection, and check that Login path (or Token endpoint for OAuth) goes straight to the service's sign-in address, not a page that forwards you elsewhere. A reply that forwards to another page isn't counted as a successful sign-in.
  2. For a login-form connection, if the service's documentation lists a different success code for sign-in, add it to Login success codes under Advanced login settings. SMTO only counts the codes listed there as a successful sign-in.
  3. Save, then select Test connection. When it shows Authenticated, run the task again. This confirms the sign-in is now recognised before the task uses it.

What success looks like

  • Test connection shows Authenticated.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who set up this connection. Don't keep re-entering the password; the type of reply, not your details, is the problem.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Authentication returned a status outside the profile's configured success codes that is not a mapped 4xx/5xx category (for example a 3xx redirect or an unlisted 2xx).

What this means

  • Authentication returned a status outside configured success_codes that did not fall into the mapped 4xx/5xx categories, including unexpected redirects or success codes. The specific receipt owns dispatch and effect truth. Authentication exchanges, resource requests and Gateway admission are separate phases; rendering this explanation performs no request and never authorizes replay of an uncertain mutation.

Why this can happen

  • Authentication returned a status outside configured success_codes that did not fall into the mapped 4xx/5xx categories, including unexpected redirects or success codes.

How to diagnose it

  • Compare the actual status with success_codes and documented redirect behavior; no credential rejection is established by this fallback.

How to fix it

  • Inspect the recorded auth endpoint status and the login recipe: point the login path at the endpoint that answers directly, or add the documented success status to the profile's login success codes. Do not assume rejected credentials without that evidence.
  • Inspect the recorded HTTP status and authentication recipe; do not assume rejected credentials without that evidence.

Retry and execution caution

  • Apply the correction and confirm the relevant state before requesting another attempt. Prior completed work remains governed by its receipts.

How to verify the fix

  • The correct endpoint returns the documented accepted status and usable session data.

What not to do

  • Do not repeatedly submit the same invalid input; correct the named constraint first.

Technical notes

  • The specific receipt owns dispatch and effect truth. Authentication exchanges, resource requests and Gateway admission are separate phases; rendering this explanation performs no request and never authorizes replay of an uncertain mutation.
